elements.title: Nanites
elements.subtitle: A swarm that learns your task

elements.text: A **nanite strain** lives in a spider-shaped capsule. On its own it can do nothing: you evolve it in the **evolution chamber**, and it becomes whatever you fed it on.

Feed it ore and you get a **miner** for the industrial miner. Dust gives a **processor** for the ore washer. A research sample gives a **scientist** for the nanite lab. The class is fixed by the first generation and never changes.
The shell colour shows what the strain is bred for: copper for copper, gold for gold, purple for crystallography.

Put the strain in the top slot, the food in the bottom one and feed it power. Every 20 seconds a **generation** passes: variants grow from the strain and the one that suits the food best stays. The strain never gets worse from it.
Ore and dust are eaten one per generation. A research sample is not eaten, it is only studied.
The graph in the window shows how affinity grows. Fast at first, then slower and slower until it hits the class cap.
Run a **heat pipe** into the chamber and generations get faster, up to four times, with bigger steps. But heat lowers the strain's stability, see the next entry.
A fresh strain has 100% stability. Each hot generation takes up to 3%, each cold one gives 2% back. It never drops below 10%.
Stability matters at work. An unstable strain slowly **wears out** in a machine: now and then its affinity loses a share. At 100% there is no wear at all.
Push the strain on heat, then take the heat away and run more generations: stability comes back and the affinity stays. That is tempering.

elements.title: Miners
elements.subtitle: More ore from the same beacons

elements.text: A miner is bred on ore or raw ore of the right material and goes into the slot on the right of the **industrial miner** window.
Affinity to a material is added to the ore: at +84% copper the miner gives 1.84 copper ore on average instead of one. The bonus needs no drill fluid.
A miner's affinities add up to +300% at most. You can breed a narrow expert on one ore or a strain with a little of everything. A miner also has a drill fluid rate, which selection slowly lowers too.

elements.title: Processors
elements.subtitle: A second product in the washer

elements.text: A processor is bred on dust. It only works in ore washers: in the regular one it goes into an upgrade slot, in the industrial one into the slot on the core panel.
For every wash of the material the strain knows, the main product has a chance to come out twice. If the output has no room, there is no extra, but nothing is lost either.
The chance grows slowly, 2.5% per generation or 3.5% on heat, and stops at 30%.
A scientist is bred on a theme sample. The sample is not eaten in the chamber. Instead of a bonus a scientist has **knowledge** of the theme, from 0 to 100%.
In the nanite lab put the scientist, the sample and **blank data cards**. The scientist writes cards on the sample's theme, one blank per card. The sample is not used up here either.
A scientist takes on a theme only from its knowledge threshold. Above it he simply writes faster: from one card a minute to one every 20 seconds.

elements.title: Species Atlas
elements.subtitle: The last tab of this panel

elements.text: Each mix of class and target is its own **species**: a copper miner, a tin processor, a crystallography scientist. A species opens when its strain gets into your inventory, and a banner slides in at the top right, like an achievement.
The atlas keeps your best record for every species and gives medals by the share of the class cap. Discoveries are yours and survive death.

elements.title: Rare Species
elements.subtitle: You do not breed them, they happen

elements.text: A rare species is a special **trait** of a strain. It appears on its own when selection runs under special conditions, and stays forever. With it the strain works better than usual.
The atlas does not say outright how to get them, it only hints. Look where something unusual surrounds the chamber: cold, heat, strong fields or a lot of patience.
Traits show up in the strain tooltip. An opened trait in the atlas shows its exact condition and what it does.
